sha: SET-AT-LAUNCH: branch veto-retry (1f6efef, from 80b3bbd) rebased onto the fleet sha at launch
notes: VETOES HOLD A THIRD OF FLEET TIME. Both engines, 24 h to 2026-09-29 12:35Z, 60 bots on 80b3bbd: 48,536 of 121,174 decisions (40.1%) vetoed by admission, holding 456 of 1,439 bot-hours (31.7%); 44.5% followed by the SAME key because the next prompt says THAT the bot was refused, not WHAT. REPLAY before building (the fleet model on the warm spare 10.0.0.16; the deployed system prompt rebuilt and HASH-VERIFIED against the fleet's system_hash for board/hive/placebo): feedback changed the action 97% vs 58% without, 0 invalid. THE CHANGE: one retry in the same tick for repeat_loop/learned_avoid/cooldown/deposit_*/bad_args, the model told what was refused and why; a retry aimed at the SAME target (count/blocks ignored, gather item->block folded) is refused without the gate; the gate checks a retry with { retry: true } -- no probation bump, no streak, no forced admission (Claude review found the double count against the real gate; a real-gate test proves the original action's sequence is unchanged). Reviewed by Claude and Codex independently; all findings fixed. 12 tests, mutants killed, 204/204. A BEHAVIOUR change: full reads; the tripwires Codex required are REVERT lines, each judged against its own baseline (a dry run showed hive pools at ~9x control's forced share on unchanged code).

licence.note: The baseline has no veto retry. ~40% of decisions are vetoed, so a 5-bot pool writes hundreds per hour.

require.name: pools whose bots are being vetoed into standing down

draw_exposure.note: Vetoes live in the decision stream, which drawexposure cannot count; _livelock_not_fixated (11,438/day fleet-wide) is the skill-stream row a veto streak writes.

own_lines.note: TRIPWIRE (Codex): forced admissions rising more than 2x faster on the canary than on control, each against its own pre-window -- the double count the Claude review found. Judged only on >= 10 canary forced admissions (null otherwise).
TRIPWIRE (Codex): the fleet endpoint .72 is shared by 80 bots; the canary's p95 decision latency > 1.5x control's means the extra calls queue.

primary.note: Items/bot-h DiD (NOISY: an unchanged pool swung -21.6 in 3 h in the dry run -- read at 26 h, not 3), executed decisions/bot-h DiD, vetoed share DiD, retry result mix and retry-admitted share. Harm from immobiledid (two-death floor, gather_ratio). Fleet-wide promotion needs a capacity check on .72 first (up to +40% calls).

harm.note: Unchanged: the two-death floor (OWNER 2026-09-11) and gather_ratio < 0.43 of control, from immobiledid.

teardown.note: THREE STEPS: drop-ins, clear canary_pool, restart the pool's bots 12 s apart; then confirm the live versions.
